subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a first-class distributed agent runtime split now, and if so should the first approved phase be local per-agent lifecycle, subagent execution backends, or a full Gateway/runtime protocol?
rationale: The current gap is real and operator demand is visible, but the durable path changes core Gateway, security, session, message-delivery, config, and deployment contracts that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep Canonical RFC And Phase It
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, approve a narrow phase order, and require security/session/protocol proof before landing runtime-boundary changes.

options.title: Narrow To Subagent Backends
options.body: Treat the current execution-backend work as the near-term scope and defer full per-agent Gateway/runtime separation.

options.title: Defer Distributed Runtime
options.body: Keep using multi-gateway profiles, hot reload, and sandbox backends while declining new distributed runtime surface for now.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical RFC And Phase It
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, approve a narrow phase order, and require security/session/protocol proof before landing runtime-boundary changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source and docs history for the Gateway runtime model, protocol docs, agents CLI surface, and config reload behavior route most strongly through this owner signal.
